findings.claim: Basis: a scratch copy of the frozen loop-3 export (HEAD 6e6bccab; lab.json sha256 0c680786, tests/lab.mjs sha256 1cc3d198), npm ci in tests, Node v24.2.0. The shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The critic wrote its own solution from the README and the topic pages; it passes 26/26 under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT, and its result lines equal expected/solved-summary.txt. Each variant below is a one-change edit of that solution, evaluated by calling every exported rule in tests/lab.mjs (the functions the 26 tests assert on); node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT on every one of the 108 variants gives the same pass counts. Runtime claims were checked with FastAPI TestClient and httpx 0.28.1 against a local stub api, and run blocks under bash -e with a stub docker and a dummy value. The loop-2 SME variant suite (113 variants plus its base) was rerun on the loop-3 and the loop-2 grader; every difference falls in the rules reworked in loop 3 (reviews-listen, reviews-timeouts, reviews-auth-forward, ci-secret-refs, ci-no-secret-prints, ci-permissions), and each is in the direction the loop-2 reconciliation asks for. New false failure introduced by the loop-3 outgoingCall rewrite. httpxClients (line 297) takes the bound name from the word directly before the equals sign, so a client bound by an annotated assignment (a name, a type annotation naming httpx.Client, then the constructor) is recorded under the annotation word instead of the variable name; and the callee pattern (line 311) needs a name followed by a dot and the verb, so a get called directly on a freshly constructed client is never a call. In both cases outgoingCall returns null and tests 24 and 25 fail with "make the call to the shop api with httpx, as the starter does" (line 327) and "no httpx request to the shop api was found" (line 383), although the code makes that request. Reproduced as one-change variants of the critic's solution: (1) a module-level client bound by annotated assignment, built with base_url set to API_BASE_URL and the Timeout, whose get takes the relative path and a dict-literal Authorization header: 24/26 (the loop-2 grader gave 25/26, failing only test 25, so the test 24 failure is new); (2) a chained client built with the Timeout whose get takes the API_BASE_URL f-string and the dict-literal header: 24/26 (26/26 on the loop-2 grader). Runtime (FastAPI TestClient, httpx 0.28.1, stub api): both forward the caller's token and answer 401 without one, so both messages are false. Severity low, not the medium given to the loop-2 URL-variable false failure: neither shape is the page's own, the starter's or the README's, and the chained form leaves the client unclosed. Under a narrow reading neither is among call-list shapes c1-c7; an annotated assignment is arguably "bound by assignment", so the reconciler may instead hold ops-sme-010 and ops-sme-008 open on it.
findings.recommendation: In httpxClients accept an optional type annotation between the bound name and the equals sign, and treat a verb called directly on a freshly constructed httpx Client or AsyncClient as an outgoing call whose client arguments are that constructor's. Keep the no-call message for code with no httpx request at all.

Runtime claims were checked with FastAPI TestClient and httpx 0.28.1 against a local stub api, and run blocks under bash -e with a stub docker and a dummy value. The loop-2 SME variant suite (113 variants plus its base) was rerun on the loop-3 and the loop-2 grader; every difference falls in the rules reworked in loop 3 (reviews-listen, reviews-timeouts, reviews-auth-forward, ci-secret-refs, ci-no-secret-prints, ci-permissions), and each is in the direction the loop-2 reconciliation asks for. New false failure introduced by the loop-3 heredoc rule. The heredocs() pattern (line 619) keeps as the opening command only the text before the heredoc operator and discards the rest of the opening line, so when cat opens an unquoted heredoc and its output is piped, on the same line, into docker login with the username variable and --password-stdin, the pipe into docker login is lost, and the exemption at line 643 (last stage docker login --password-stdin) cannot fire for a cat-opened heredoc piped into the login. Reproduced as a one-change variant of the critic's solution: the login step's run replaced by that cat-heredoc-into-login pipeline, whose heredoc body is the step-env variable mapped from secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD. Test 7 fails with "a run step writes a secret (directly, through an env variable or encoded) to the run log"; it passed test 7 on the loop-2 grader. Under bash -e with a stub docker and a dummy value, the value reaches only docker's stdin and nothing is printed, so the message is false. Test 6 also fails it ("the password piped to docker login must be an env variable mapped from secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD"), identically on the loop-2 grader, so only the test 7 failure is new. Severity low: the shape is not taught and test 6 already rejects it. Under a narrow reading it is not h5 ("a heredoc fed to docker login --password-stdin"), because the heredoc is fed to cat; the reconciler may instead hold ops-sme-r2-03 and ops-sme-r1-07 open on it.
findings.recommendation: Capture the remainder of the opening line after the delimiter and test the joined pipeline (the text before the heredoc operator plus that remainder) for a last stage of docker login --password-stdin before flagging a cat-opened heredoc body.

The critic wrote its own solution from the README and the topic pages; it passes 26/26 under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT, and its result lines equal expected/solved-summary.txt. Each variant below is a one-change edit of that solution, evaluated by calling every exported rule in tests/lab.mjs (the functions the 26 tests assert on); node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT on every one of the 108 variants gives the same pass counts. Runtime claims were checked with FastAPI TestClient and httpx 0.28.1 against a local stub api, and run blocks under bash -e with a stub docker and a dummy value. The loop-2 SME variant suite (113 variants plus its base) was rerun on the loop-3 and the loop-2 grader; every difference falls in the rules reworked in loop 3 (reviews-listen, reviews-timeouts, reviews-auth-forward, ci-secret-refs, ci-no-secret-prints, ci-permissions), and each is in the direction the loop-2 reconciliation asks for. Low residual on message class only; no false pass or false fail remains. Guard list must-pass, each 26/26 and run against the stub api (header forwarded with a token; g1-g6 answer 401 without one, g7 answers 422 because FastAPI rejects the missing required header before the handler runs): g1 not-authorization with status_code=401 first; g2 detail first and status_code=401 after; g3 401 positional, status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, and the constant positional; g4 is None and == None; g5 a positive check (truthiness, and is not None) wrapping the call with else raising 401; g6 a positive check building the headers with else raising 401 and the call after (also with a URL variable and in the c6 async shape); g7 a required parameter with no guard. Must fail, each only test 25: f1 print-only guard, f2 HTTPException without raise, f3 guard returning a dict and f7 positive check whose else returns a dict all get the missing-raise message (line 399), which is true for each: at runtime none answers 401 without a token (f1 and f2 end in 500 when httpx rejects the None header value and the api receives nothing; f3 and f7 answer 200 without calling the api). f4 inline and through a name, the no-guard dict-literal shape and f8 (guard after the call) get the no-guard message (line 400). f5 gets the forward message (line 384). The failing clause: the guard list assigns f6 (a positive check with no else) the no-guard message, but line 399 returns the missing-raise message whenever any positive check exists (line 394). Reproduced with two f6 shapes (headers built under a positive check with the call after, which at runtime reaches the api with no token; and a print-only positive check with the dict-literal call, which ends in 500), and the same holds for the ops-edu-06 no-guard form named under ops-sme-010. The text "your missing-token check does not raise HTTPException with 401 ... raise it there" points the learner at their positive check, where a 401 would refuse callers that do send a token. Fix: return the line 399 message only for a negative guard or a positive check that has an else branch, and the line 400 message otherwise.
